supported_scope: Run builds or tests, inspect failures, and revise work based on results within the Antigravity CLI workspace
unestablished_scope: Automatic defect correction or revision based on test results
Direct integration with external build systems beyond local test commands
required_setup: Configure workspace with a test suite and optionally set toolPermission and enableTerminalSandbox in settings.json; use execution modes (default, accept-edits, plan) to control file write approvals; optionally enable terminal sandbox for safe command execution
constraints: Workspace must have a test suite ready for verification loops
File write and command execution permissions governed by toolPermission settings or /permissions rules
Execution modes affect approval behavior for file modifications
Terminal sandbox restricts filesystem and network access for safety

evidence.section: CLI best practices > Establish verification loops
evidence.quote: The single most effective way to ensure reliable, correct modifications from an autonomous agent is to provide the agent with a local verification mechanism (such as unit tests, build commands, or formatting scripts). Before asking the agent to implement a code change, follow these steps: Ensure your workspace directory has a test suite ready. If tests don’t exist, direct the agent to write a stan
evidence.claim: Supports running tests and inspecting results to verify work

evidence.quote: /diff Utilities — Open the interactive diff viewer to view changes, turns, and commits.
evidence.claim: Provides interactive diff viewer to inspect changes and revisions

evidence.section: Choose an execution mode > Available modes
evidence.quote: default Pauses for interactive diff review before modifying or creating files. Standard development, reviewing sensitive code changes, and careful refactoring. accept-edits Automatically approves file edits and creations (mkdir, touch, file writes). Rapid prototyping, iterating on trusted code, and reducing prompt interruptions.
evidence.claim: Execution modes control approval of file modifications during build/test cycles

evidence.section: Terminal sandbox > Antigravity CLI > How it works
evidence.quote: With the terminal sandbox enabled, Antigravity CLI executes commands inside an OS-level isolation boundary. Commands can write to your workspace, temporary directories, and common build caches, and read system directories such as /usr and /etc so your tools keep working.
evidence.claim: Supports safe execution of build and test commands within a sandbox
